text: Danish SU: a full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules. Check su.dk before budgeting.

Health insurance is legally mandatory for residents in Abu Dhabi and Dubai, and universities normally include a compulsory scheme in the fees — NYUAD lists mandatory health insurance inside its direct costs. Healthcare is private, modern and expensive without cover. Your Danish EHIC does not apply.

EU citizenship gives no advantage. Danish citizens receive a visa on arrival as visitors, but you cannot study on that. Your university sponsors a student residence visa, which involves a medical fitness test (including a chest X-ray and blood test) and an Emirates ID. The visa is tied to the institution: if you leave the university, the visa is cancelled. Some students qualify for the UAE's five-year student 'golden visa' for outstanding academic performance.
Denmark’s SU works differently for a full degree outside the EU/EEA. Check su.dk before budgeting.

The UAE is socially conservative by Danish standards. Laws on alcohol, relationships outside marriage and public behaviour differ from what you are used to, and enforcement varies by emirate. Read the Danish foreign ministry’s travel advice properly, not the marketing brochures.
Danish SU can in many cases be taken abroad for a full degree - check with SU Styrelsen first, as this is usually the biggest single source of money.

Health insurance is compulsory. With a Danish EHIC you are covered for necessary treatment, but for a full degree you will normally want proper Austrian cover: students who are not covered through a parent or a job can take out student self-insurance with the OeGK. Register with an Austrian insurer soon after arriving and carry your e-card. Student self-insurance with the OeGK costs 78.84 EUR a month in 2026.

As a Danish (EU) citizen you have free access to the Austrian labour market with no permit and no hour cap; you are limited only by tax and social-insurance thresholds for marginal employment. Non-EU students with a student residence permit can be given a work permit for up to 20 hours a week, without a labour-market check; the employer applies for it (OeAD).

Work out which route your state uses. For New South Wales and the ACT you may apply through UAC on one application and one fee; for Victoria, South Australia and Western Australia the state admissions centre will not take an IB candidate sitting the exams in Denmark, and Queensland's is unresolved, so you apply directly to each university.
Danish SU may in some circumstances support a full degree abroad - check su.dk and ask your studievejleder well before you apply.

UAC converts an IB Diploma into a Combined Rank, which it states is comparable with the ATAR for tertiary entrance in every Australian state and territory. There are two schedules on one page and they give different answers. Candidates who sat the IB in Australia from November 2022 are converted from a fine-grained IB Admissions Score in quarter-point steps; everyone else, including anyone sitting the May session in Denmark, is converted from the whole diploma score out of 45. The schedule underneath both is agreed nationally by the Australasian Conference of Tertiary Admissions Centres and re-determined every February.

Read the right table. The IBAS schedule is the more precise-looking one and it is not yours: it converts 24.00 to 64.40 where the table that applies to a Danish candidate converts 24 to 64.60, and the gap widens in the thirties.
Three-year bachelor's degrees, so you finish in the same time as in Denmark, and four-year honours only if you choose it.

"Le concours d'entree est organise une seule fois par an, le jeudi 27 aout 2026", at Brussels Expo, in person only, 09h30 to 17h00 with no admission after 10h30. Results followed on 4 September 2026. The rule for 2027 is that results come within three days of the jury's deliberation and at most ten days after the examination. Two structural points a Danish candidate needs: non-residents compete for a capped share of places, 15 per cent for medecine and dentisterie and 20 per cent for sciences veterinaires, and you may sit the concours in at most two different academic years within any five-year period, with sittings from 2023 onwards already counting.

The one nationality-specific deadline KU Leuven states in plain text, and it is good news: "For Dutch-taught programmes, the deadline for non-EEA applicants is 1 February. EEA applicants applying for a Dutch-taught programme are not subject to a deadline." As a Danish citizen you are in the second group. It says nothing about English-taught programmes, which are handled per programme.
Danish SU taken abroad is the main source of support for a Danish student - apply to Uddannelses- og Forskningsstyrelsen before you leave.
Flemish study grant (studietoelage) is available to students who meet Flemish residence and means conditions; a student newly arrived from Denmark will usually not qualify in year one.

Bring your European Health Insurance Card from Denmark. If you stay for a full degree, Belgium will normally expect you to join a Belgian health insurance fund (mutualité / ziekenfonds) - registration is cheap, sometimes free for students, and it is what makes reimbursement of GP and hospital costs work in practice. Universities usually have a designated fund they work with and will help you sign up during enrolment. Non-EU students must show proof of health cover to get their residence permit.
Flanders: Study in Flanders states that most qualifications obtained abroad do not grant direct admission and are assessed individually, so allow time for the equivalence or admission decision.

Belgium is two higher education systems in one country. Dutch-speaking Flanders (KU Leuven, Ghent, Antwerp, VUB, Hasselt) and French-speaking Wallonia and Brussels (UCLouvain, ULB, Liege, Mons) each have their own ministry, fees, rules and calendar. Tuition for an EU student is low - 1,181.40 EUR for a full year in Flanders in 2026/27 - and the universities are genuinely strong. The honest problem for an IB student from Denmark is language: almost all Belgian bachelor's degrees are taught in Dutch or French, and the fully English-taught bachelor's offer is small. Master's programmes are a different story, with hundreds in English.

The OUAC's wording is exact and it is the whole of the answer: "There is no specific Undergraduate application deadline if you are a Group B applicant. Deadlines vary at each university and sometimes depend on the program." It adds the warning that costs people places: "You must ensure the OUAC has enough time to process your choices before the universities' program deadlines" — so the university's date is not the date you can submit on. Do not take the OUAC's own headline dates for yours. 15 January 2027 and 28 May 2027 are published on the same page under Group A, which is an applicant currently taking Ontario high school courses and under 21 — not a Danish IB candidate. The University of Toronto's own dates are separate entries below; every other Ontario university sets its own, so read it on that university's page. The OUAC page was last updated on 14 September 2026, and its dates sit inside collapsed sections that open when clicked.

Published as "Out-of-country applicants (except US and A-Level applicants): Deadline to submit your final transcript to confirm your offer of admission." That is the row for a Danish IB candidate; the 30 June date on the same page is for US and Canadian applicants. UBC decides on interim grades reported by your school and uses the final IB results to confirm the offer and any first-year credit, so request the electronic transmission from the IB in the spring so that it goes the day results are released, about 6 July 2027.

McGill states it with the year and the weekday attached — "Friday, January 15, 2027" — as the "Application deadline for Fall 2027 admission to undergraduate programs by applicants studying or who last studied in an overseas or U.S. high school", which is the group a Danish IB candidate is in. No closing time is published on that page. McGill assesses on predicted IB results or, if you have them, on final ones.

Published as "FALL ENTRY (September) Deadline: March 1", with no year, so 2027 is expected rather than confirmed. It is the date a Danish student sees first on Concordia's page, and it is the wrong one: the international date is 1 February, four weeks earlier.

Two months before UBC's general January deadline, and an easy date for a Danish applicant to miss: it is the date by which an international student must have applied to UBC and submitted the award application to be considered for the International Scholars Program. The scholarship is the reason the date exists, and the scholarship is the thing that is gone on 16 November — the general admission route stays open until 15 January. Published with a time and a time zone, 11:59 p.m. PST, which is 08:59 the following morning in Denmark; a Danish applicant working to a local midnight has until the morning of 16 November, but do not use that margin.
Not applicable - Canada has no EU/EEA fee category. Danish students pay international fees.
Danish SU may in some circumstances support a full degree abroad. Check the rules on su.dk and talk to your studievejleder early.

Health cover depends on the province, and the difference is large. Ontario leaves international students outside the public plan altogether and enrols them in UHIP instead, which is a cost for the whole degree. British Columbia, Alberta and Nova Scotia all admit international students to their provincial plans, each on its own condition and each after a wait during which you need private insurance. Quebec requires continuous health and hospitalisation cover for the entire study stay as a condition of the CAQ. The EHIC and the Danish yellow card are not valid anywhere in Canada.

Most universities guarantee residence to first-year students who apply by a separate housing deadline, usually in spring. Take the guarantee - Vancouver and Toronto private rentals are very expensive and finding a room from Denmark is very hard. From second year most students share a house or flat, which is where the real cost appears.
Winters in Montreal, Toronto, Edmonton and Calgary are far harder than a Danish winter. Vancouver and Victoria are mild but very wet.
holders of a foreign certificate who do not need a visa, which includes Danish and other EU citizens

UZH publishes "1 January until 30 April" as the ordinary autumn-semester window, "1 May until 31 July" as an extended window available for Swiss qualifications only, and "1 January until 28 February" for applicants who need a visa. A Danish citizen needs a residence permit rather than a visa, so 30 April is the deadline that applies - and the extended July window, which would have let you apply after results, is the one you cannot use. UZH also requires German at C1.
Decide on the teaching language early. German at C1 or French at B2 is a year or more of work, and it is the requirement most Danish IB students underestimate.

There is no EU/non-EU split in Switzerland - the split is between students with Swiss residence or citizenship and everyone else. A Danish student moving from Denmark counts as a foreign student. At ETH Zurich that means CHF 2,190 per semester rather than CHF 730.
Danish SU can in many cases be taken abroad for a full degree - check with SU Styrelsen, because Swiss living costs make this the decisive factor.

Swiss basic health insurance is compulsory for residents, but the federal health office says students from EU/EFTA countries do not have to take it out as long as they are not working: they are covered by their home system and treated on the European Health Insurance Card. If you start working you must take out Swiss insurance. Cantons handle the formalities, so register your EHIC cover with the cantonal authority in your first weeks as your university's international office directs.
EPFL applies lower thresholds to Swiss applicants (36 points and grade 5/7 in maths and physics) than to everyone else, so the 38-point bar is the one that applies to a Danish student.

ETH doubled down on international students: from autumn semester 2025 the tuition for foreign students is CHF 2,190 per semester against CHF 730 for Swiss residents. Coming straight from Denmark, you pay the higher rate.
Language, not grades, is what stops most Danish IB students: ETH teaches bachelor's in German, the University of Zurich requires German at C1, and EPFL requires French at B2.

China has no UCAS, no Common App and no ministry-run deadline for international undergraduates. The gaokao, which is the national examination the whole Chinese calendar bends around, is not a route a Danish IB candidate takes at all; international applicants are admitted by each university under its own 申请-审核 (application and review) procedure, on its own dates. Two things follow that the rest of this page depends on. First, every date below belongs to one institution and nothing generalises from it. Second, China runs two intakes — a September one, which is the main one and the one this page covers, and a separate February or March spring intake which a smaller number of programmes offer. "2027 entry" on this page means September 2027 unless an entry says otherwise, and a deadline you find on a Chinese university's site may belong to the spring intake and be eight months out of step with the one you want. Check which intake a date is for before you plan around it. Note also that China's joint-venture universities — Duke Kunshan, NYU Shanghai, Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool, Nottingham Ningbo, CUHK-Shenzhen, United International College, Wenzhou-Kean — run on an entirely different calendar from Tsinghua, Peking, Fudan and Shanghai Jiao Tong, and several run on the American one.

Published with its full calendar year on DKU's English international-admissions site as "Early decision application deadline: November 2, 2026 (11:59pm ET)", which is 05:59 on 3 November in Denmark. Applications are made through the Common App, which DKU began accepting for the 2027 entry term in August 2026, and Early Decision on the Common App is binding: you may hold one Early Decision application only, and if admitted you withdraw the rest and enrol. DKU's own How to Apply page does not restate those terms, so the binding force comes from the Common App agreement you sign rather than from anything DKU publishes — read it before you file. There is no application fee. The CSS Profile is required if you are seeking financial aid, and DKU is test-optional for the 2026-2027 cycle. A warning that matters more than any of this: DKU runs two entirely separate admissions tracks on the same domain. The Chinese-language site (admissions.dukekunshan.edu.cn, 中文 – 中国学生) publishes a 综合评价 comprehensive-evaluation route with rounds closing 3 January and 5 February, for Chinese students. Those are not your dates. A Danish applicant uses the English site marked "English – International Students", and DKU states that international applicants must be non-Chinese citizens.

The Chinese Government Scholarship is applied for by one of three routes with three different calendars: Type A through the Chinese embassy in your country, Type B directly to a CSC-designated Chinese university, and Type C through certain international organisations. Each embassy and each university sets its own closing date, so there is no single deadline. www.campuschina.org, the China Scholarship Council portal that embassy notices still name, did not resolve on 23 or 24 September 2026, and the Chinese Embassy in Denmark's English site carried no scholarship notice on either day. From October 2026, watch the embassy's announcements for the 2027/2028 notice and ask each university for its Type B date.

Published with its full calendar year as "Regular decision application deadline: January 4, 2027 (11:59pm ET)", which is 05:59 on 5 January in Denmark. Not binding: you keep every offer you hold and reply on 1 May 2027, which is its own entry below. The DKU application is the Common App plus two DKU-specific essays, and DKU also lets an applicant to Duke University in North Carolina share that application with DKU — but only the materials submitted at that moment are shared, and transcripts, school reports, recommendations and CSS Profile documents that arrive later must be sent to both universities separately. That is the detail most likely to cost somebody an assessed application.

International students are normally required to buy a specified Chinese medical insurance policy as a condition of registration, and to pass a medical examination as part of the residence permit process. Public hospitals are inexpensive but crowded; international clinics in Beijing and Shanghai are good and expensive. Your Danish EHIC does not apply.

China is two systems for a Danish IB student: English-taught joint universities, and Chinese universities that teach mostly in Chinese. The Sino-foreign joint universities — NYU Shanghai, Duke Kunshan, XJTLU, Nottingham Ningbo, CUHK-Shenzhen, BNBU and Wenzhou-Kean — teach in English, award a foreign or joint degree and admit on their own or the American calendar. The Chinese universities, such as Tsinghua, Peking and Zhejiang, admit international students by application and review, teach mostly in Chinese, and from 2026/2027 require a new national test, the CSCA, before you apply.
Denmark's SU works differently for a full degree outside the EU/EEA. Check su.dk before budgeting.

Not published: the faculty's table is headed "Entrance examination dates and venues for 2026" and has not rolled over. Two features of the 2026 list matter enough to carry forward. First, four sittings late in the season - 18, 19, 25 and 28 August 2026 - were marked as open only to applicants who are EU citizens or hold a valid residence permit, which is an advantage a Danish candidate has and a non-EU candidate does not. Second, the examination can be taken only once per academic year, so the date you pick is the only attempt you get.

The central page carries only a range - English-taught bachelor's and master's deadlines "vary for each faculty (from February till June/July)" - and it is stamped as last changed in May 2023, so it is three years stale and names no faculty. Mathematics and Physics closed 30 April 2026; the Third Faculty of Medicine 15 April 2026; Plzen 30 April 2026; Hradec Kralove works differently, with 30 April 2026 for its online sitting and 7 May 2026 for sittings held abroad rather than one global deadline; and the First Faculty of Medicine ran to 5 September 2026. None has published anything for 2027/28. Judging by this cycle, expect them from November or December 2026, faculty by faculty, on each faculty's own site rather than centrally. Charles also states that it has no rolling admissions and grants no individual extensions.

Published as "1 December-31 July (for EU residents)". Non-EU residents get a shorter window closing 31 May. As a Danish citizen you have the longer one, which runs well past your IB results. Masaryk publishes this window with a day and a month but no year at all, and no academic-year heading anywhere on the page, so the year here is projected onto the September 2027 intake. Where the page's summary table and its per-faculty sections disagree, go by the faculty section, which gives the opening dates the table leaves out.

Danish SU for a full degree abroad, at DKK 7,426 a month before tax for students living away from home in 2026. Czechia is not a Nordic country for SU purposes, so support is capped at four years — worth thinking about if you are planning a six-year medical degree.

Bring your Danish EHIC. It gives you medically necessary care from public providers on the same terms as a Czech insured person. The national portal is clear that the EHIC is not travel insurance — it generally does not cover private clinics, repatriation or travel losses, so supplementary cover is sensible. Whether an EU student also needs to register with a Czech health insurer such as VZP is not addressed on the official pages; ask your university.

This is a real advantage over a Danish studentereksamen. The automatic-equivalence list covers the European Baccalaureate, the IB, and school-leaving certificates from Slovakia, Poland, Hungary, Slovenia and Germany. Denmark is not on it, so a studentereksamen would need either regional nostrification at 1,000 CZK or a university assessment at 950 to 990 CZK.

The broadest English-taught bachelor's menu outside Prague, priced from 3,000 to 14,000 euros depending on programme, and the one institution that runs its medicine entrance exam through a centre covering Denmark — Interstudium in Oslo, with dates in March, May, June and July. It also gives EU citizens the June and July exam slots that non-EU applicants cannot use, which means you can sit it after IB results. Its medicine waiver needs 35 points with 19 from HL Biology, HL Chemistry and Physics, and unlike Charles 2nd Faculty it appears not to accept predicted grades.
SU — studies abroad
Charles Faculty of Medicine in Hradec Kralove - Admission process (30 April online, 7 May abroad)

Since 1 March 2025 an IB Diploma is exempt from nostrification in Czechia by law. That matters more than it sounds: a Danish studentereksamen is not on the automatic-equivalence list and would have to go through a regional authority or pay a university assessment fee, while your IB Diploma is simply accepted. The other thing to know is that studying in Czech is free for everyone, regardless of nationality — the fee depends on the language of instruction, not on your passport. English-taught tuition runs from around 500 euros a year at the agricultural university to 24,250 for medicine at Charles.

None of these faculties lists an entrance-exam venue in Denmark. For Charles 2nd Faculty the nearest dated overseas sittings are London (2 July 2027) and Berlin (13 July 2027); Oslo is listed but has no 2027 date yet. Plan on London or Berlin, an online sitting, or travelling to Czechia.

A lead time, not a date anyone publishes, which is why it carries no day. uni-assist states that you "will usually receive your evaluation result in 4 to 6 weeks", counted from the day it receives your online form, and that applications are evaluated in order of arrival. Its regional table - keyed to where your certificates were issued, not where you live - puts "Western Europe and Latin America: 3-4 weeks", the slowest band on the list, which is the one a Danish IB diploma falls into. The VPD section itself gives no processing figure at all and says only to apply as early as possible. uni-assist's own recommendation is to apply "at least 8 weeks before the deadline expires" so that it can tell you in time if a document is missing. With IB results on 6 July and a 15 July university deadline, that is impossible to do on results - so start the uni-assist file in spring 2027 with predicted grades and school documents.
Danish SU can in many cases be taken abroad for a full degree - check the rules with SU Styrelsen before you commit, because this is usually the largest single source of money.

Health insurance is compulsory and you cannot enrol without proof of it. As an EU student with a Danish EHIC you can usually apply to a German statutory insurer for an exemption (Befreiung), which they confirm electronically to the university - do this before enrolment day. If you take a job in Germany or your EHIC does not cover you, you join German statutory student insurance instead, which in 2026 costs about 137-161 EUR a month: 87.38 EUR plus the insurer's own additional contribution, plus 30.78 EUR long-term care insurance (35.91 EUR if you are 23 or over and childless). Confirm the current rate with the insurer.
German citizens who studied abroad without German in the IB must prove German knowledge before enrolling, under section 1e of the KMK agreement.

As a Danish (EU) citizen you have full access to the German labour market with no permit and no hour limit - you are only limited by tax and social-insurance thresholds for student jobs. Non-EU students on a residence permit under section 16b of the Residence Act may work 140 full days or 280 half days per calendar year, or alternatively up to 20 hours a week during the lecture period, a rule in force since 1 March 2024. Source: https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/aufenthg_2004/__16b.html

100 euros at Tallinn University, non-refundable, covering up to two programmes. A Danish student pays it — the waivers are for people educated in Estonia, Estonian citizens, long-term residence holders and, for the 2026/27 intake, Ukrainian citizens. Other institutions' fees are not confirmed here; check each one.

Danish SU for a full degree abroad, at DKK 7,426 a month before tax for students living away from home in 2026. Estonia is not a Nordic country for SU purposes, so support is capped at four years (48 SU-klip), with no extra SU if you are delayed.

Estonian performance stipends, the need-based study allowance and the Estonian student loan are not confirmed here — whether a Danish citizen in an English-taught programme qualifies for any of them is unknown. Do not count on them.

This is the one thing students get wrong. Enrolling at an Estonian university does not give you Estonian health insurance — international students are not covered by the Health Insurance Fund unless they are employed or hold permanent or long-term residence. Bring your Danish EHIC, the blue card, and understand that it covers public treatment at Estonian rates with the same patient co-payments Estonians pay, and nothing private. Supplementary cover is sensible. Emergency services on 112 are free and available around the clock, and specialists including psychiatrists, dentists and ophthalmologists can be seen without a referral. Taking a part-time job is one way into the state system.

The only technical university in Estonia, with around 11,000 students, and the single best-value option in the country for a Danish student: two English-taught engineering degrees that cost EU citizens nothing while non-EU students pay 6,000 to 7,000 euros. Its deadlines, entrance tests and the exact conditions attached to the free places are not confirmed here. Its admissions page on 23 September 2026: international applicants prepare their application in DreamApply; Estonian citizens and long-term residents apply through SAIS.

Tallinn University states it most clearly: students who have completed International Baccalaureate studies can submit their graduation documents as proof of English proficiency, so no IELTS is needed. It also exempts anyone who completed previous education fully in English in an EU or EEA country, which covers a Danish IB school. If a test is required, it asks for IELTS Academic 6.0 with at least 5.5 in each component, Cambridge B2 First, C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency at 169 overall, or PTE Academic 59. Estonian Business School asks for English at at least B2.
Estonian-language programmes at public universities are generally free through state-funded places, but they are not a realistic route for a Danish school leaver.
SU — hvad kan du få (SU til en hel uddannelse i udlandet)

Estonia has a reputation for teaching in English, and at master's level that is true. At bachelor's level it is not. The official national listing names 27 English-taught bachelor's degrees in the entire country, one of them with no current intake, so your menu is short and you should treat it as a list to read end to end rather than a system to search. The one genuinely striking offer is at TalTech, where Cyber Security Engineering and Integrated Engineering are free for EU and EEA citizens — as a Danish student you would pay nothing for either.

Enrolling at a university does not give you Estonian health insurance. International students are not covered by the health insurance fund unless they are employed or hold permanent residence — bring your Danish EHIC and consider supplementary cover.

The one Spanish date that is safe to carry forward, because UNED states it as a standing annual rule rather than a calendar entry: "El plazo para solicitar la acreditación de UNEDasiss on line, se abre el 4 de febrero y se cierra el 1 de diciembre de cada año". The 1 December end is misleading on its own and UNED says so in the next sentence: the accreditation has to exist before the university admission round closes in early July, and UNED asks for the request "como mínimo, 6 semanas antes del cierre de inscripción universitaria". It has three months in law to process a request and says the usual turnaround is three weeks from receiving form, payment and documents together. Add postal time: UNED states that documents posted from abroad take more than 15 working days to arrive. And avoid the shutdowns - UNED is closed 29 March to 6 April 2026, 1 to 15 August 2026, and 24 December 2026 to 7 January 2027.
Send the documents: passport copy, compulsed copy of the IB Diploma, compulsed copy of your last two years’ grades. Posted from abroad they take more than 15 working days to reach UNED.
Danish SU may be taken abroad for a full degree if the programme is approved — check su.dk before committing.

As a Danish citizen you travel on your passport or ID card. If you stay more than three months you register in the Registro Central de Extranjeros and receive a green EU registration certificate with a NIE number. You need the NIE for a bank account, a phone contract and usually for enrolment itself, so apply for an appointment as soon as you arrive. You will also normally register on the local padrón at the town hall.
100 euros, but only for applicants who are not EU/EEA/Swiss citizens. A Danish student pays nothing.

The student healthcare fee is 35.35 euros per term at the 2026 rate. Kela says you do not have to pay it if you have social security coverage in another EU/EEA country: as a Danish student on your EHIC you send Kela a copy of the card instead. Kela does not send a bill either way.

Danish SU for a full degree abroad. Because Finland is a Nordic country, SU and SU loans are paid as if you studied in Denmark. Under the SU reform that takes effect on 1 January 2027, anyone starting a degree after 1 July 2025 gets SU for the programme's prescribed length only; the extra twelve months some older pages still mention no longer apply to you. You must be a Danish citizen, or an EU/EEA citizen who can document sufficient ties to Denmark, and the programme must be officially recognised in Finland. Apply in minSU Fast Track no later than the first month you want support for.

Bring your Danish EHIC, the blue EU card. Degree students at universities and universities of applied sciences can use FSHS/YTHS, the Finnish Student Health Service, provided you are registered as attending for the current semester. Kela states that a student with social security coverage in another EU/EEA country does not pay the student healthcare fee, and shows the EHIC at FSHS instead.

The IB and the European Baccalaureate are the only foreign certificates that count for certificate-based selection wherever they were taken. German Reifeprüfung and DIA only count if completed in Finland. Oulu states in plain English that an IB Diploma earned abroad qualifies.

Small, Swedish-speaking and right in central Helsinki, which makes it an unusually easy cultural landing for a Dane. An IB Diploma puts you in its 7–21 January 2027 joint application for the business and engineering degrees; only the Reifeprüfung/DIA has to be completed in Finland.

Home of the 6G Flagship programme. It also has the most IB-friendly wording of any Finnish university: it states in plain English that an IB Diploma earned abroad qualifies for certificate-based selection, which exempts you from the SAT.

Finland's Swedish-language university, and closed to you at bachelor level unless you can read and write Swedish — though as a Dane your Swedish may be closer to adequate than most applicants', so it is worth asking. Its master's degrees in international law and human rights and in peace mediation are among the most distinctive in Europe. Åbo Akademi does not mention the IB anywhere on its English bachelor pages.
Finnish and Swedish-taught degrees are free to everyone regardless of nationality, but they are not realistic for a Danish school leaver.
Åbo Akademi teaches every bachelor's degree in Swedish and requires documented Swedish. A Danish student's Swedish may in practice be good enough — worth asking them directly.

As a Danish citizen you do not apply to Migri and you do not need a residence permit. You register your personal data with the Digital and Population Data Services Agency at dvv.fi. This is simpler than the standard EU registration that other EU citizens have to do, and it is the correct route for anyone from Denmark, Iceland, Norway or Sweden. Non-EU students need a continuous type A residence permit for studies over 90 days, granted for the whole degree: 600 euros electronically, 750 on paper, or 400 and 430 for minors.
SU — the SU reform in English

Finland converts your IB transcript into points on published tables that differ by field of study, and admits you on them directly. It is called todistusvalinta, certificate-based selection, and it means you can skip the SAT and skip entrance exams at most universities. The main door is a single joint application at Studyinfo, open 7-21 January 2027 for degrees starting in August 2027, with up to six ranked choices. As a Danish citizen you pay no tuition at all, in any language of instruction.
No tuition for EU/EEA citizens, including every English-taught bachelor's degree. A Danish student pays nothing.
Finland counts as a Nordic country for Danish SU, so you get SU and loans exactly as if you studied in Denmark, not the four-year cap that applies outside the Nordics.

A major research university on the German border, in a bilingual city that is also home to the European Parliament. Unistra's main site is in French; its English guidance for applicants from abroad is at international-welcome.unistra.fr, which is where the admissions link points.
Lyon is a far cheaper city than Paris, and emlyon's BBA lets you spend up to 75% of it abroad; first-year fees for the 2027 intake are €15,500 a year.

As a Danish citizen you need no visa and no residence permit. Travel on your passport or national ID card. There is no compulsory EU registration in France, but you will need a French bank account (for CAF and rent), a French phone number and a social-security number, so start those in your first weeks. Non-EU students apply for a VLS-TS student visa through the Études en France procedure before departure.
France is a short train or flight from Denmark, so visiting before you commit is realistic

The LNAT dates page runs a separate late route for international applicants who send the UCAS form by 30 June 2027: book the test slot by 25 July 2027 and sit it by 31 July 2027. As a Danish applicant this is the only LNAT window still open after the January deadlines have passed, so it is worth knowing it exists — but it depends on the law course still having places.

University of Glasgow 2027/28: Arts and Social Sciences GBP 28,275; Science, Engineering, Nursing and Medical/Veterinary/Life Sciences GBP 33,708; Veterinary Medicine and Surgery GBP 38,670 (Medicine MBChB and Dentistry BDS listed as TBC). Glasgow 2026/27 for comparison: Arts and Social Sciences GBP 27,720; Science and Engineering GBP 33,210; Medicine MBChB GBP 62,730; Dentistry BDS GBP 58,500. Across the sector a realistic 2026/27 planning range for a Danish IB student is roughly GBP 22,000-40,000 a year for a normal degree, and GBP 45,000-70,000 a year for clinical medicine.
Danish SU can in principle be used for a full degree abroad if Uddannelses- og Forskningsstyrelsen approves the programme. This is the single most important thing to check with your studievejleder.

You pay the Immigration Health Surcharge of GBP 776 per year as part of the visa application. That gives you access to the NHS on the same basis as a UK resident for the length of your visa. Register with a local GP when you arrive. An EHIC or the Danish yellow card does not replace this.

Almost all UK universities guarantee a place in university accommodation to first-year international students who apply by the stated deadline, which is usually in the summer once you have firmly accepted an offer. This is much easier than the Netherlands or Denmark. Apply the moment your firm choice is confirmed.

Decide which route you are taking. For a Danish IB student there are three, and they are genuinely different: an English-taught programme at a public university, a Greek-taught public place through the Ministry’s foreign-nationals category, or a private English-language college such as ACG/Deree.
Danish SU for a full degree abroad requires programme approval by Uddannelses- og Forskningsstyrelsen - check with your studievejleder.

As a Danish EU citizen you have the right to live and study in Greece and will normally register locally for stays over three months. Non-EU students need a student visa and residence permit. The specific Greek procedures, documents and timescales are not confirmed here - the Study in Greece visa page directs non-EU students to a third-party visa service rather than setting out the rules.

Greek public universities teach almost entirely in Greek, and entry for Greek-speaking students runs through the national Panhellenic examinations. A growing number of public universities now also run separate English-taught bachelor's programmes with tuition fees, applied to directly on the IB, and these are the realistic route for a Danish IB student: about twenty were listed on the Study in Greece platform in September 2026, at €4,500–€17,000 a year. Beyond that there is the private, American-accredited college sector.
